text:
marta: Customer ACME Inc opened a dispute — huge token spike on 2026-03-03. They saw ~2.3M tokens billed, claim our client retried on upstream 502s and doubled requests. Asking for provisional credit and root cause.

devon: Do we have request_ids or any request-level logs? can we correlate with 502s in the infra logs?

marta: Uploaded initial logs + customer screenshot to the case folder (link). They included a client-side stack trace and their SDK version (redwood-sdk v1.4.0).

anika: Quick update — I repro'd locally with v1.4.0. When the server returns a 5xx, the JS/py SDK retry logic resends the whole payload without an idempotency key. Repro steps are tiny:
```
# python repro (simulated 502)
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key="x")
try:
  client.generate(prompt="hello")
except Exception:
  # SDK retries by default and resends tokens
  pass
```
The second send consumes a full token count again.

devon: That matches an infra blip we had at 03:12 UTC — five upstream 502s for the model pool in us-west-2 (ops incident 762). Correlation looks strong.

marta: Customer provided timestamps of retries matching our 03:12 window. They're pretty upset, want immediate provisional credit so their bill isn't overdue.

samir: Finance here — how big is the duplicate portion (tokens / $)? We need numbers for revrec and a recommended provisional credit. Also need a short revrec note format we can drop into the ledger.

anika: From sampling logs, duplicate tokens ~= 1,234,000 tokens. Using their pricing tier that's about $4,520. Exacts pending full export. Patch ready: PR adds idempotency-key header when retries happen and toggles conservative retry-on-502. PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/987

devon: I'll export a per-request CSV (request_id, timestamp, model, tokens) for the affected account and flag duplicate_counts. ETA 45m.

marta: I told the customer we can apply a provisional credit while we audit. They agreed to a provisional credit but asked for a written note and expected timing.

samir: For accounting: use revrec reference RC-20260303-ACME-1. GL account 6100 (cost of services) for the adjustment until final determination. Please attach the CSV and sign-off from support. We also need the invoice number this offsets.

marta: Invoice INV-2026-03-03-ACME is the one. I uploaded the CSV export to GDrive: https://drive.example.com/ACME-dup-tokens.csv and added a short support sign-off.

kevin: Support manager here — confirmed. Apply provisional credit $4,520 as a hold while engineering finishes audit. @samir please create the revrec entry and finance note.

billing-bot: PROVISIONAL CREDIT APPLIED: acct=acme-123 amount=$4,520 ref=CR-1867001234 created_by=marta

samir: Got it. I'll create the revrec memo and provisional journal today, code RC-20260303-ACME-1, will tag in NetSuite. Once engineering finalizes the audit we'll either finalize credit (refund/adjust invoice) or reverse.

anika: Follow-up: I'll ship the SDK fix in a patch release (v1.4.1) within 2 hours and backfill a monitoring regression to alert on duplicate token patterns. Also adding an opt-in idempotency header for customers.

marta: Closing internal loop — case escalated to finance + eng. Customer notified of provisional credit and ETA for final audit. I'll update the case when CSV is posted and when final numbers are confirmed.

devon: CSV export posted, contains per-request counts and dedup flags (see GDrive link in the case). If anyone needs a different format ping me.

samir: Once we have final confirmation, I'll post the revrec entry ID here. For now ledger holds RC-20260303-ACME-1 with provisional credit CR-1867001234.

kevin: Thanks team. Action items: anika -> release patch, devon -> finalize CSV, samir -> provisional revrec, marta -> customer comms.

marta: Noted. Will follow up with a short customer note and final timeline. :white_check_mark:
